subject.title: [Feature]: Stop Burying Your Agent's Soul: Configurable Context File Elevation

question: Should per-file bootstrap elevation and Project Context exclusion be accepted as a core typed config surface, or should this be solved through a documented plugin/context-engine contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the durable API affects prompt authority, prompt-cache stability, public config shape, and the core-versus-plugin boundary called out by VISION.md and AGENTS.md.

options.title: Extend plugin/context-engine contract
options.body: Document or add the minimal external API needed for a plugin or context engine to elevate and exclude bootstrap files without adding another core config knob.

options.title: Add narrow core config
options.body: Accept a typed core config for ordered pattern-to-section elevation with explicit exclusion behavior, schema/docs alignment, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep flat Project Context
options.body: Leave current rendering as-is and direct users to existing context-engine additions, bootstrap hooks, or manual prompt customization.

recommendation.title: Extend plugin/context-engine contract
recommendation.body: Document or add the minimal external API needed for a plugin or context engine to elevate and exclude bootstrap files without adding another core config knob.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter posted the latest maintainer-side framing for this exact product/API boundary and has recent prompt/docs history on the affected surface.
